goal.title: 11 · A cube of 24 bits
goal.text:
A datum cube holds three bytes, red green blue. Each face carries four tiles, one bit each: +x and −x hold red (high nibble, low nibble), +y and −y green, +z and −z blue. On each face the top-left tile, seen from outside, is the nibble's highest bit. White is 1, black is 0.

Make c1 orange, #ffa500: red ff (all eight tiles on ±x), green a5 = 1010 on +y and 0101 on −y, blue 00. Then step back more than 12 cells: the cube becomes one pixel of its color.

steps.text: Click c1 to select it, then click a tile on its +x face. The tile turns white: bit 23 is on, the top bit of red.
Turn on every tile of +x and −x: red is ff. The inspector (E) shows all 24 tiles; clicking one there toggles it too.
Set green to a5 on +y (1010) and −y (0101), keep blue off, then fly or walk more than 12 cells away: the cube is one flat orange pixel.
Press Check to see the stars.
